items.title: The hotels
items.text: Howard Johnson is one of Wyndham Hotels & Resorts’ economy brands: **304 properties** and 43,998 rooms at December 31, 2025, of which 133 are in the United States. More of the rooms are in Greater China (26,456) than in the U.S. (10,119).[^16]

items.title: The restaurant name
items.text: Eater reported in 2017 that Wyndham owns all the relevant Howard Johnson’s trademarks, and that only a former franchisee reopening on an original site, or Wyndham itself, could put the name on a restaurant again.[^13] No restaurant uses it today.[^14]

items.title: The company-owned restaurants
items.text: Marriott kept 418 of them in 1985 and said many would become Big Boy outlets. It still owned 90 at the end of 1987 and 50 in mid-1991, when Franchise Associates bought 17.[^1][^2]

items.title: The last building
items.text: The Lake George restaurant went up for lease in late 2021. CNN reported that the listing for the 7,500 square foot building stated a price of $10.[^14] What has happened to the building since is not covered by our sources.

items.title: The recipes
items.text: Franchise Associates said in 2001 that it owned the original recipes and had licensed manufacturers to make the ice cream and other signature products for shops and grocery stores.[^5] Whether any of these are still made is unknown to us.

items.title: Ground Round
items.text: Imperial kept the 210-unit Ground Round chain out of the 1985 sale because Marriott did not want it.[^1][^2] Its later history is outside this page.

blocks.title: Who owned the name
blocks.subtitle: After 1985 the trademark and the restaurants had different owners.

nodes.what: Buys the Wollaston store and puts his name on the ice cream. Sole owner until the 1961 listing.[^1]
Listed with 605 restaurants. The family sells shares through the 1960s.[^1]
The British tobacco and brewing group buys the whole company, agreed in September 1979.[^1][^2]
Buys the company without Ground Round, keeps 418 company restaurants for conversion and passes the name on at once.[^2]
Takes the trademark, 125 company lodges, 375 franchised lodges and 199 franchised restaurants.[^2]
The franchisees’ own company gets an exclusive license for restaurants and signature foods. By 2007 the franchise rights are with La Mancha Group.[^5][^7]

nodes.owner: Blackstone affiliate, later HFS and Cendant
nodes.what: Prime sells the Howard Johnson and Ramada systems and files for Chapter 11 that September. Hospitality Franchise Systems becomes HFS, then Cendant in 1997.[^1][^26]
Spun off from Wyndham Worldwide. Franchises 304 Howard Johnson hotels. No restaurants.[^16]

blocks.source: International Directory of Company Histories[^1], Los Angeles Times[^2], Franchise Associates[^5], Hartford Courant[^7], Wyndham’s 2025 Form 10-K[^16]. The “bankrupt” marker on the 1990 step refers to the seller, Prime Motor Inns, not to the Howard Johnson brand.
